title: Article 226 PIL — High Court Writ Jurisdiction and Other Public Purposes (Art. 226)

content.overview: Article 226 is the High Court gateway for PIL. It may enforce fundamental rights and other legal rights for any other purpose, subject to territorial limits and bona fide public-interest standing. Private disputes dressed as PIL fail.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Fundamental or other legal right? (2) Territorial competence? (3) Bona fide public interest? (4) Prefer 226 or 32? (5) Abuse markers?
content.study:
Core rule: Article 226 is wider than Article 32 in rights enforceable — fundamental rights and other legal rights — within the High Court's territory.

Liberal standing still requires bona fides. Prefer 226 for region-specific wrongs and non-Part-III public duties; prefer 32 for Supreme Court Part III enforcement.

Aligned with companion thin topic art-226. Case-law verification remains separate.
